findings.title: Traits already on the item sort into the '(not applicable)' group, and choosing one adds a second copy
findings.detail: CanApplyTo returns false when an active trait has m.def == this, so a trait the item already has is sorted to the bottom and labelled '(not applicable)'. AddTrait has no duplicate guard (it rolls and appends), so choosing it stacks a second copy. This only affects the debug menu. If you want the label to say why, check comp.HasTrait(d) in the Select and label those '(already applied)'.

findings.title: Traits switched off in settings sort as applicable with no marker
findings.detail: The sort key is only CanApplyTo, and the action passes ignoreDisabled=true, so a trait the player switched off appears in the applicable group. EntadApi.GetApplicableTraits leaves these out (EntadSettings.IsDisabled). A '(disabled)' suffix would make the menu match what random generation would pick. Opinion-level polish, not a defect.
